header:
Date: 2028-03-28
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Arjun Rao (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO, Northvale), Marcus Hale (Platform Eng, Northvale), Sonia Li (SRE, Northvale)
Recording: cloud.fireflies.link/rec/ff-20280328-nv-01 (internal only)
summary: Discovery focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency for streaming responses, and hosting decision (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Northvale needs sub-1.5s p95 for short assistants and 200-400ms p95 for small inference endpoints; they also expect burst workloads of ~5k concurrent users during peak. Discussed benchmark plan and next steps to validate token/sec and prefix caching benefits.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
KV/prefix caching and warm vs cold starts
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll keep this tight, want to understand your latency goals and hosting constraints.
[00:12] Lena (Northvale CTO): Thanks Maya, yeah. We're evaluating whether Redwood Hosted can meet our p95 before we talk Dedicated or Private. Main constraint is customer-facing assistants — need about 800-1500ms p95 depending on prompt size. For batch/rerank endpoints lower is ok.
[00:30] Arjun (Redwood SE): Got it. When you say 800-1500 ms p95, is that for end-to-end including network and client RTT, or just server-side generation?
[00:38] Marcus (Northvale): End-to-end from our edge -> Redwood -> back. We have some CDN+API gateway latency ~80-120ms typical. So server target is a little lower.
[00:50] Sonia (SRE): Also we have stringent data residency needs for EU traffic — some customers must remain in EU region.
[01:02] Maya: Noted. We can route by policy — region pinning or dedicated pools in EU. Any requirements for on-prem or air-gapped?
[01:11] Lena: Not initially, but for certain regulated customers we might require Private later. So minimum requirement: Hosted works now if it meets p95 targets and has KMS for encryption-at-rest.
[01:22] Arjun: For streaming, two dimensions: sustained throughput (tokens/sec) and concurrency (number of simultaneous streaming connections). What's your expected concurrency and token speed per stream?
[01:33] Marcus: For assistants, typical stream is 150-400 tokens, we expect 30-80 concurrent sessions in normal peaks, but during promotions we estimate spikes to 2.5k concurrent sessions for a ~10 minute window.
[01:49] Maya: OK. Spikes like that are important because Hosted has burst capacity but Dedicated gives more predictable throughput.
[01:57] Arjun: Quick clarifying question — are those spikes multi-region or single region?
[02:02] Marcus: Mostly single-region (US-East). Some EU peaks but smaller.
[02:06] Sonia: Also we have SLA requirements — p95 must be under 1.5s for the assistant flow; otherwise we pay credits to customers.
[02:15] Lena: Right, so cost vs latency tradeoff matters. We want to understand unit cost numbers if we move to Dedicated vs Hosted.
[02:23] Maya: We'll share a baseline cost sheet. For performance, we recommend running a token/sec streaming benchmark with your prompt set — we'll simulate both Hosted and Dedicated-like capacity.
[02:34] Marcus: What about prefix/KV caching? We have common prompts — can caching reduce your p95 alot?
[02:41] Arjun: Prefix caching helps a lot for assistant-style repeats. In our internal perf we saw 30-60% per-token latency reduction for cached prefixes, depends on model and sequence length. There is warm/cold behavior — first request goes through cold path.
[02:58] Speaker 1: (inaudible) kv cash, uh cache, mm hmm.
[03:05] Sonia: Cold starts worry us — does Redwood have keep-warm or pinned containers?
[03:11] Arjun: Dedicated pools can keep kernels and KV caches hot, plus we have autoscaling policies with warm pools to reduce cold-start tail. For Hosted, we maintain warm capacity for common models but less predictable during huge spikes.
[03:25] Lena: Could you give an example p95 numbers for a 1k-token request on Hosted vs Dedicated?
[03:31] Arjun: Rough numbers — using a 70B open model family example: Hosted cold-start p95 for 1k tokens could be 2.5-3s; warm path ~1.1-1.6s. Dedicated optimized with pinned warm kernels ~0.9-1.2s p95 depending on quantization and batch config. These are model-dependent but give an order of magnitude.
[03:51] Marcus: And what about token/sec per stream for streaming, like how fast tokens come back? We need snappy partial responses — 50-250 tokens/sec seems to be the range we care about.
[04:02] Arjun: Yes, token emission rate is a combination of model compute and your network buffer. On modern GPUs we're seeing 150-300 tokens/sec for smaller models in streaming when batch size is 1 and KV cache is used. For larger models with attention-cost, it's lower.
[04:18] Maya: We should run your prompts through a microbenchmark — measure p95, median, throughput, and tokens/sec under concurrency 50, 250, 1000 to see behavior.
[04:29] Marcus: How do you handle fallback when Dedicated capacity is saturated? We can't have 5s tails for customers.
[04:36] Arjun: We have routing policies: fall back to a compatible model variant (smaller quantized model) or route to Hosted spare capacity. You can configure automatic fallback thresholds and graceful degradation.
[04:48] Lena: What's the overhead of fallback in terms of prompt compatibility and output quality?
[04:53] Arjun: There's a small quality delta — we recommend cross-evals on a holdout prompt set. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and smaller model candidates and show expected quality impact.
[05:06] Sonia: Security — can you integrate with our KMS and support SSO for role-based access?
[05:11] Maya: Yes, we support KMS integrations (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/HSM) and SAML SSO with RBAC. We'll share the SOC2 and KMS docs.
[05:19] Marcus: For Private deploy, how different is the control plane and where do logs live? We need audit logs in our account for PCI compliance.
[05:27] Arjun: Private deployment puts the control plane in your VPC; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM and stored in your cloud account. We support HSM for key custody.
[05:36] Lena: Good. About the benchmark itself, define what you need from us.
[05:40] Arjun: We need a representative prompt corpus (Lena), expected token lengths distribution, and preferred concurrency scenarios. We'll run 3 iterations for each concurrency point and provide latency histograms, p95/p99, and token emission profiles.
[05:53] Marcus: We'll provide 600 example prompts, with token lengths from 80 to 1.2k. Is that enough?
[05:59] Arjun: Perfect. Also please flag which prompts are streaming-critical (partial replies important) vs ones that can be synchronous.
[06:07] Sonia: Network— we need a test harness that can run from our VPC to your Hosted endpoint to measure e2e. Can you support a test agent in our VPC?
[06:15] Maya: For Dedicated/Private we can spin a test runner in your VPC. For Hosted we'll provide a synthetic runner from a controlled region, but it's ideal if you run a runner inside your network for true e2e.
[06:26] Lena: Cost question — if we need to size Dedicated for steady state 100 concurrent streams with spikes to 2.5k, what's typical commit?
[06:33] Arjun: Many customers combine Dedicated for steady base capacity and use Hosted burst for spikes. Dedicated sizing usually based on sustained tokens/sec; we can propose a Dedicated pool to cover 100 concurrent with 200 tokens/sec per stream as baseline, then estimate extra for burst. We'll include autoscale & burst licensing in the cost sheet.
[06:50] Marcus: Latency SLOs — can you expose p95 at route level and alert on regressions?
[06:55] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route p95 dashboards, trace links, and we can instrument custom metrics and alerts.
[07:03] Lena: Any showstoppers for us? I worry about cold-start tails during spikes and cost cliff for Dedicated.
[07:10] Arjun: We mitigate with warm pools, prefix caching, and fallback routing. Cost cliff can be smoothed with autoscale policies + Hosted burst. We'll run the benchmarks to quantify risk.
[07:20] Marcus: Also want to confirm EU data residency — can we pin models to EU-only hosts?
[07:25] Maya: Yes, you can pin by region and by pool for Dedicated/Private. Hosted also supports region routing.
[07:31] Sonia: One minor transcription note — your earlier doc said KV cache but audio said KV cash, ignore that.
[07:36] (laughter)
[07:40] Maya: Quick recap, we'll: 1) Arjun runs benchmarks with your prompts across concurrency scenarios; 2) Maya shares cost/pricing and SOC2/KMS docs; 3) schedule VPC network deep-dive with Sonia.
[07:52] Lena: Sounds good. If benchmarks align we'll pilot Dedicated with warm pools for the busiest region.
[07:58] Maya: Great — I'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc links (pricing + security).
[08:03] Marcus: Thanks all.
[08:06] End of recording.
